items.title: *** EDPS-Civil Society Summit: safe by design, not by exclusion – reclaiming our digital future ***
items.description: *** EDPS-Civil Society Summit: safe by design, not by exclusion – reclaiming our digital future *** Each year, the EDPS is organising an EDPS-Civil Society Summit during @ edri # privacycamp26 . @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski took part in the discussion with Luísa Franco Machado from EquiLabs in a roundtable facilitated by Simeon de Brouwer from EDRi. The session focused on the @ EUCommission proposal for the EU KIDS Act to explore the limits of measures based on exclusion or invasion of privacy, and to analyse the underlying structures and business models that expose all users to harm and vulnerability. Wojciech Wiewiorowski stressed that protecting children online must be a priority, but that the way we do it matters. Children are not only people to be protected, they are also holders of rights, including the right to express themselves, to access information, to have their privacy and personal data respected. But mostly, kids need to prepared for what comes next. Any interference with their rights must be necessary and proportionate under the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. “Protection should not mean exclusion. Protection is about managing risks, not banning participation

items.title: *** Brussels Privacy Symposium 2026: My Data is Mine ***
items.description: *** Brussels Privacy Symposium 2026: My Data is Mine *** Cookie banners, AI training and anonymisation: three key topics in the GDPR and ePrivacy reform. @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski took part in a discussion at Brussels Privacy Symposium on the ongoing GDPR and ePrivacy reform. He recalled that the EDPS and EDPB strongly supported the aim of tackling consent fatigue and cookie banner proliferation, while ensuring a high level of fundamental rights protection. On the Digital Omnibus, he noted that the EDPB Opinion on AI models had already opened the door to relying on legitimate interest for responsible AI development. “I have said this before and will say it again: the Digital Omnibus should be about fostering responsible innovation, not a dilution of core concepts or safeguards of data protection law.” Wojciech Wiewiorowski added.

items.title: *** Future of Privacy Forum – 2026 EU Regulator Award ***
items.description: *** Future of Privacy Forum – 2026 EU Regulator Award *** The Future of Privacy Forum, a global non-profit focused on data protection, AI, and emerging technologies, today announced the recipients of its 2026 Awards honoring outstanding contributions to data protection and privacy in Europe. The awards were presented during the Awards night held on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of the Brussels Privacy Symposium, bringing together leaders from the EU data protection community to celebrate a decade of dialogue and progress in the field. @ Supervisor Wiewiorowski: “I am very honoured to accept this 2026 EU Regulator Award on behalf of the entire European Data Protection Supervisor team. It recognises our collective commitment to safeguarding fundamental rights, ensuring accountability in the use of personal data, and promoting responsible innovation in an increasingly digital world. Behind every piece of personal data, there is a person, with their own rights, dignity and expectations. As new technologies reshape our societies, keeping this human dimension at the heart of data protection remains essential to building trust in Europe.”

items.title: ⚠️ A phishing link clicked, a telephone number leaked, fraudulent messages… these are some of the risks linked to personal data breaches.
items.description: ⚠️ A phishing link clicked, a telephone number leaked, fraudulent messages… these are some of the risks linked to personal data breaches. According to the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity or # ENISA Threat Landscape 2026, public administration was the most targeted sector in the EU 🇪🇺 in 2025. EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (EUIs) must notify us of personal data breaches. Between January and August 2026, we received 98 notifications from EUIs, of which 91 were admissible. How can you or your institution 🔎 recognise, 🚫 prevent and 🧐 mitigate cyber threats that can lead to personal data breaches? Check our factsheet for more information on common cyber threats and follow us to learn more about privacy risks during # ECSM . 🔧 Discover more here: https:// link.europa.eu/M6fRQt

items.title: *** 4th AI Act Correspondents Network Meeting ***
items.description: *** 4th AI Act Correspondents Network Meeting *** The @ EDPS is holding today the fourth meeting of the # AIAct Correspondents. The network brings together correspondents from all EU institutions, bodies and agencies, and functions as a forum for cooperation and fostering a common understanding of topics on AI governance. @ EDPS_supervisor welcomed participants to the meeting, which this time focuses on the transparency of AI systems, the EDPS AI regulatory sandbox pilot project and the EDPS Compass for AI. @ Secretary_General Cervera-Navas took the stage to deliver the opening remarks. He reported on the appreciation expressed by the Secretaries General of the EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies in response to the establishment of the network and its activities. # AI # Governace # Sandboxes # Regulation

items.title: A human in the loop is not always the same as a human in control.
items.description: A human in the loop is not always the same as a human in control. Marking European Cybersecurity Month, the @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiórowski writes on two aspects sides of the human factor, which is the most common cause of personal data breaches but often seen as the final safeguard over automated decisions. What people need is the same in both cases: 📚 training, 💡good information, ⏰ time to review and ⚡the authority to act. Read the blogpost: https:// link.europa.eu/VYVdV7 # CyberSecMonth # ECSM

items.title: *** Are we underestimating the economic value of privacy? ***
items.description: *** Are we underestimating the economic value of privacy? *** "For a decade, the debate has focused on what data protection costs, with little attention to what it is worth". At an event organised by BEUC - The European Consumer Organisation, Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski delivered closing remarks welcoming efforts to make a change. He recalled the EDPS's long-standing position that personal data is not a currency and that a fundamental right cannot be treated as a commodity, a position the EDPS has held from its 2017 Opinion on digital content contracts to its recent Opinion on the proposed Digital Networks Act. "The question is not whether we can afford privacy. It is whether we have ever properly counted what we lose without it," Wojciech Wiewiorowski said. 📃 Read the full speech here: https:// link.europa.eu/jKC7CM

items.title: *** Keynote speech at the 2nd High-Level Roundtable on Equality Data ***
items.description: *** Keynote speech at the 2nd High-Level Roundtable on Equality Data *** Counting inequality is the first step to tackling it, provided the data is collected responsibly. @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski delivered a keynote speech at the 2nd High-Level Roundtable on Equality Data, organised by the @ EUCommission with the support of the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU 2026. The event brought together policymakers, equality bodies, statistical offices, civil society, academics and EU institutions. He welcomed the forthcoming Council Recommendation on equality data collection, but urged participants not to let it become the finish line. The Supervisor outlined six principles for a future framework: legal legitimacy, meaningful participation, robust data protection safeguards, purpose limitation and proportionality, algorithmic accountability, and equity in access. He also underlined that data protection is not an obstacle to legitimate policy objectives, but the foundation on which they can be pursued with public confidence. items.title: 📩In your inbox: the EDPS Newsletter, with a raft of new opinions and a look at emerging tech
items.description: 📩In your inbox: the EDPS Newsletter, with a raft of new opinions and a look at emerging tech Welcome to the latest edition of # EDPS Newsletter. Since last time, we have published 13 opinions, formed a new partnership with the European Law Institute and taken a closer look at two technologies that will shape data protection in the years to come. Read and get informed on: 🧮 A new # TechDispatch on secure multi-party computation, the cryptography that lets organisations compute a shared result without ever seeing each other's data. The report explores what this means for compliance. 🔐 The leap to post-quantum data protection, the focus of our latest # IPEN event, co-hosted with the Paris Lodron University of Salzburg. Quantum computers may still be years away, but data stored today could be decrypted later. 🤝 Our new institutional membership of the European Law Institute (ELI) Institute, signed in Paris by @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski and # ELI President Teresa Rodríguez de las Heras Ballell. ⚖️ Three opinions on the European Commission's package of reforms in justice and home affairs, covering Europol's processing of operational data, the modernisation of Eurojust, and a targe

items.title: *** Global AI Privacy Forum 2026 ***
items.description: *** Global AI Privacy Forum 2026 *** Today, @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski took part in the Global AI Privacy Forum 2026, hosted by the Personal Information Protection Commission(PIPC), Republic of Korea under the theme "Privacy for Innovation, Partnership for Cooperation". He joined the special session "Readiness Powered by Cooperation", which focused on practical capacity building for privacy regulators facing rapidly evolving AI, with particular attention to emerging and developing data protection authorities. The Supervisor stressed that capacity building is a precondition for effective AI supervision. Authorities need to share legal and technical expertise and operational tools, and to pool their limited human, technical and financial resources. For the EDPS, this is a practical question: it combines its role as data protection authority for the EU institutions with new responsibilities under the AI Act. Capacity building should be at the centre of international cooperation. "No DPA needs to develop every capability alone. items.title: *** RAID conference ***
items.description: *** RAID conference *** Supervisor @ EDPS_supervisor spoke on the panel "Growth & Simplification – The AI and Digital Omnibuses and beyond" at the RAID (REGULATION - AI - INTERNET - DATA) conference in Brussels. He underlined that simplification can support, rather than weaken, protection when it makes obligations clearer, reduces unnecessary duplication and helps organisations comply more effectively with the EU digital rulebook. Not all simplification requires new legislation. Much can already be achieved within the existing framework through cooperation structures, such as the DMA High-Level Group, with a more consistent and operational guidance, including European Data Protection Board Joint Guidelines, and common templates and methodologies at EU level, such as those the EDPB is developing for DPIAs, ROPAs and privacy notices. The Supervisor also stressed that regulators can only deliver if their mandates are matched by resources and expertise. The EDPS has called for a Digital Clearinghouse 2.0 to bring regulators from different fields together. items.title: *** # ECSM 2026 kicks off ***
items.description: *** # ECSM 2026 kicks off *** This year’s European Cybersecurity Month launched today at @ Curia Massimo Attoresi, Deputy Head of Unit, Technology and Privacy at # EDPS delivers a keynote speech on the human factor in cybersecurity, 2026's focus. 📊 The numbers tell a story: of 115 personal data breaches notified to the EDPS so far in 2026, half are the result of cyberattacks. The first time they've been the leading cause. Many of these breaches begin with the person sitting at the keyboard. # AI is being used to augment attacks, making phishing and social engineering harder to spot and putting personal data at greater risk. While technical defences matter, resilience is built by people who are trained in cybersecurity and empowered to act. 🛡️Our position is that strong cyber defence begins with obligatory training for management as well as for all staff on the digital front lines. "The most resilient organisation in Europe will be the one where every employee, from the newest intern to the most senior official, feels equipped, trusted and genuinely responsible for the security of the organisation and the protection of the fundamental rights of any individual" added Massimo💡. items.title: *** 24th meeting of the Central and Eastern Europe Data Protection Authorities ***
items.description: *** 24th meeting of the Central and Eastern Europe Data Protection Authorities *** Today, at the 24th meeting of the Central and Eastern Europe Data Protection Authorities (CEEDPA) in Zadar, the @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiórowski spoke about the challenges of assessing the impact of AI systems on data protection and fundamental rights. As AI Act Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIAs), Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) and cybersecurity risk assessments increasingly intersect, Wojciech Wiewiórowski stressed that they are not interchangeable and that the AI Act does not set aside existing data protection or cybersecurity frameworks. “The real measure of compliance is not whether an organisation completed compliance forms. It is whether those assessments improved how the AI system is designed, deployed, monitored, and governed, and whether fundamental rights are genuinely protected as a result” said the Supervisor. Finally, he also underlined the importance of making the assessments work together coherently, while avoiding the risk of treating fundamental rights as a procedural checklist. # FundamentalRights # AI # AIAct

items.title: *** AI and competition law - Lunch Talk at Columbia University ***
items.description: *** AI and competition law - Lunch Talk at Columbia University *** Earlier this week, Leonardo Cervera-Navas, EDPS Secretary-General, and Sonia Pérez Romero, Head of AI Unit, took part in a Lunch Talk at Columbia University dedicated to competition law and AI. The discussion was led by Professor Lina Khan, head of the newly established Center for Law and the Economy at Columbia University, and co-hosted by Professor Anu Bradford, Henry L. Moses Professor of International Law and Organizations at Columbia Law School. The Secretary-General highlighted the EDPS’s longstanding work on the links between data protection, competition and consumer protection, and spoke about the EDPS's more recent role under AI Act. In his intervention, Leonardo Cervera-Navas stressed that “Data Sovereignty will be crucial in the discussion about attracting AI capabilities in Europe. Through the GDPR the European Union has positioned itself as the continent with the best data quality in the world”. Sonia Pérez Romero said: “Market Surveillance Authorities under the AI Act have two immediate objectives: to ensure strong AI Governance and supporting responsible innovation. items.title: *** Meeting at the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency ***
items.description: *** Meeting at the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency *** On 23 September, on the margins of the 4th Annual Meeting of the Central and Eastern Europe Data Protection Authorities, @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiórowski met Zdravko Vukić, Director of the Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP). The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss ways to strengthen cooperation and share knowledge between the EDPS and AZOP. Cooperation and the exchange of experiences are key to promoting consistent data protection across the EU. # DataProtection # Privacy # DPAs # Cooperation

items.title: *** Visit to EMSA ***
items.description: *** Visit to EMSA *** Earlier this week, the @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiórowski, visited the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) in Lisbon. During the visit, he exchanged views with Dominika Lempicka-Fichter, Head of Department Corporate Services, Radostina Nedeva-Magerlein, EMSA Data Protection Officer, and Andrea Tassoni, Head of the Executive Office. The visit included a presentation of EMSA’s work and an exchange of views and good practices on data protection.

items.title: *** AI red lines: from prohibition to enforcement ***
items.description: *** AI red lines: from prohibition to enforcement *** On 23 September, EDPS Secretary-General, Leonardo Cervera-Navas participated in the panel “AI Red Lines – From Prohibition to Enforcement”, co-organised by the Minderoo Foundation and the Center for AI and Digital Policy at the margins of the High-Level Week of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. The discussion focused on how governments can enforce AI red lines through clear prohibitions, independent oversight, democratic accountability, and by ensuring that humans remain in control of AI systems. “Establishing clear, robust and enforceable rules is not about stifling innovation. It is about ensuring that innovation does not come at the expense of fairness, transparency, safety or public trust,” said the Secretary-General. He also highlighted that the AI Act draws a firm, non-negotiable line between technological innovation and fundamental rights: “Today, as a supervisory authority, our mandate is clear: prohibited AI practices are a red line, and enforcing that line is a priority, as they represent unacceptable risks.” Enforcement begins with legal certainty. items.title: *** 17th EDEN Conference on Data Protection and Cybersecurity in Law Enforcement ***
items.description: *** 17th EDEN Conference on Data Protection and Cybersecurity in Law Enforcement *** @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski delivered keynote speech at the 17th EDEN Conference on Data Protection and Cybersecurity in Law Enforcement reflecting on how far law enforcement can go in the digital domain without crossing the line that protects investigations and fundamental rights. He set out the EDPS's concerns with the proposed new Europol Regulation, part of the EU's Justice and Home Affairs package: the extended processing of data on individuals with no verified link to criminal investigations; the default treatment of biometric querying as "strictly necessary"; and Europol's proposed access to private party data without national judicial authorisation. The EDPS calls for clear, binding limits as Europol's tasks, biometric processing and shared data environments, such as the proposed Police Shared Data Space, continue to expand, alongside reciprocal supervisory powers and adequate resourcing for oversight. items.title: *** UN Digital Cooperation Day ***
items.description: *** UN Digital Cooperation Day *** This week, the EDPS Secretary-General Leonardo Cervera-Navas travelled to New York on a mission to the United Nations and Princeton University. On 21 September, he took part in the United Nations Digital Cooperation Day under the theme "A Global AI Future Through Science, Policy and Capacity" as part of the High-Level Week of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. The Secretary General joined the panel "Co-Designing a Network of Interoperable Cross-Border AI Governance Sandboxes" as a contribution to the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance, presenting the EDPS's own AI regulatory sandbox pilot and the lessons learned so far. The EDPS pilot, launched in October 2025, tests an AI system supporting job matching in EU selection procedures with the European Commission, the first of 15 EU institutions that requested to take part. In his intervention: "Transparency, accountability, and a human-centred approach are not optional; they are the foundation of trustworthy AI. items.title: *** Recap: EDPS summer Opinions ***
items.description: *** Recap: EDPS summer Opinions *** Our busy legislative work did not stop for the summer. The EDPS issued several Opinions on proposals ranging from law enforcement cooperation to cloud infrastructure, tax administration and fisheries. Four of them address a single Justice and Home Affairs package: 🚓 a transformative new regulation for Europol’s processing of operational data ⚖️ a similar revamp of the rules governing Eurojust 💻 a targeted revision of the EU Data Protection Regulation (EUDPR) 🔎 a recast of the Directive on the European Investigation Order These proposals would significantly expand what EU agencies can do with personal data in the criminal justice field. Our Opinions set out what needs to be in place for that to happen lawfully.
